summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 14, part 44) in which the narrator meets Marcella and Nikko at the Minneapolis Institute of Arts while worrying about Wheeze, who has not replied to a text. Marcella presents a loud, detailed flowchart plan for a project, and Nikko recites a Welsh poem's line that he explains is about sex, drawing a warning from a security guard. Nikko and the narrator then discuss the narrator's brother, who is held and has a lawyer named McSweeney, and an upcoming rally on Sunday for the Minneapolis Nine Solidarity Committee.
one_line: Fiction excerpt: the narrator meets Marcella and Nikko at the Minneapolis Institute of Arts, discussing a project plan, a Welsh poem, and the narrator's jailed brother.
key_facts: The narrator checked about nineteen times to see whether Wheeze had made contact, and the narrator's latest text to him was still unanswered.
The narrator met up with Marcella at the Minneapolis Institute of Arts at five past three.
Marcella had been on time and had drawn up a plan with an elaborate printed flowchart for completing the project efficiently.
Marcella's voice is always loud and robotic, and she pushes up her thick glasses when they slip down her nose.
Nikko arrived next and raised an arm, reciting the line "Light breaks where no sun shines" in a sing-song accent.
A security guard came over on squeaky shoes and gave Nikko a warning in a deep, threatening whisper.
Nikko played a recording of a Welsh poet reciting "Light breaks where no sun shines" on his cell phone, and the voice matched Nikko's own accent.
When Marcella asked what the line meant, Nikko said "Actually? It's about sex."
Nikko said quietly that he had heard about the narrator's brother and asked how he was doing.
The narrator said they would not let them talk to the brother yet, but the narrator had got him a lawyer.
The lawyer is named McSweeney, whom the narrator visited at her house and asked to take the case.
The narrator said the brother might go to prison and that the narrator was scared.
Nikko said he would be at a rally on Sunday in front of the federal building, organized by the Minneapolis Nine Solidarity Committee.
Marcella noticed that the narrator and Nikko were not paying attention to her and asked if they were paying attention; Nikko replied "At your service."
